newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., Bucs bond sale postponed again.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., Bucs bond sale postponed again.

text.p: Legal wrangling has again postponed the Tampa Sports Authority's sale of $204.5 million of revenue bonds for the new Buccaneers' stadium, the Hillsborough County Attorney said Wednesday.
The negotiated sale had been set for this week via Smith Barney Inc.
Hillsborough County Attorney Emmy Acton said it would be delayed pending a Florida Supreme Court ruling on a request for a rehearing of the court's bond validation.
"The rule requires that on validation rehearing, the court take action immediately, so we're hopeful we'll hear any day," Acton said.

Voters approved a sales tax increase to pay for the stadium and other projects in September. The bonds originally were to be issued in November but the sale was stalled when former Tampa Mayor Bill Poe sued to block the issue.
Poe said the stadium plan was unconstitutional because it would use public funds to benefit the private, for-profit football team.
The Florida Supreme Court rejected that argument and validated the bonds last month, but Poe subsequently asked the court for a rehearing. The request is still pending.
